summary: Encapsulation keeps an object's data behind methods so the object can reject bad values. Java marks fields private and gives outside code public getters and setters.
notes: private double gpa; cannot be read or changed from Main. The compiler stops it.
setGpa() throws IllegalArgumentException before gpa = value; runs, so a bad value is never stored.
The constructor calls setGpa(gpa) instead of gpa = gpa; so the same check applies when the object is made.
pitfall: Writing maya.gpa = 9.9; in Main causes the compile error "gpa has private access in Student". Use maya.setGpa(...) instead.
